findings.evidence: grep: scripts/housekeeping.py:62-64 SCOREBOARD_MARKER/SCOREBOARD_META_RE/TRUSTED_ASSOC and :114 latest_scoreboard_meta duplicate core.py:70 scoreboard_meta. The copies already differ: core uses r"<!--tauceti-meta:v1 (.*)-->" (single literal space, no re.S) while housekeeping uses r"<!--tauceti-meta:v1\s+(\{.*?\})-->" with re.S — a multi-line meta block matches in housekeeping but not in core, exactly the drift a shared module is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: Have core.py own the trusted-scoreboard fetch and let housekeeping.py import it (it can still read its own full_rounds/states fields from the returned meta), or, if unifying a human-owned file is out of this PR's single-topic scope, note the residual duplication so a follow-up consolidates it.
findings.issue: core.scoreboard_meta re-derives what scripts/housekeeping.py:114 latest_scoreboard_meta already provides: fetch issue comments, keep those with the <!--tauceti-scoreboard--> marker AND an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR author, take the newest, extract the <!--tauceti-meta:v1 ...--> JSON. The PR advertises core.py as the one place that reads PR status, yet leaves this parallel implementation untouched, so three trust-logic copies now exist and can drift.

summary: Clean consolidation of the labels+Zulip status derivation into core.py, but the "single source of truth" is incomplete: scripts/housekeeping.py already derives the same trusted-scoreboard state independently, and the two copies have already drifted on the meta regex.
